description: We are a team of passionate students interested in technology, innovation, and space. Our skills include programming, AI/ML, data science, research, and prototype development. We aim to build practical solutions for NASA Space Apps challenges and welcome teammates interested in AI/ML, web development, UI/UX, GIS, astronomy, and data visualization.
summary:
EmberScope is an AI-assisted research dashboard that turns NASA microgravity combustion data into traceable fire-safety insights. Built for the Flame in Freefall challenge, it helps researchers explore investigations, compare experimental conditions and prioritize evidence for spacecraft, space stations, lunar and Martian habitats, and pressurized rovers.

The app imports 22 experimental tables from NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics repository, preserving 2,009 source rows alongside a 24-entry catalog. It combines 15 research profiles with visual comparisons of oxygen, airflow, materials, gravity and reported outcomes. A modeling workspace prepares source-linked datasets, while configured AI models support semantic ranking and evidence-grounded explanations.

EmberScope highlights prevention, detection and suppression research, including potential Earth applications. It separates observations from interpretations, flags missing data and links conclusions to original sources. The prototype supports research discovery and exploratory modeling; it does not certify fire safety. Its licensed open-source foundation and AI-assisted development are disclosed.
details:
EmberScope addresses NASA's Flame in Freefall challenge through a researcher-focused workflow: Explore, Compare, Insights and Report. It helps users investigate fire prevention, detection and suppression while preparing traceable datasets for flammability modeling.

The application connects NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository with NASA publications and investigation overviews. Its reproducible snapshot includes 24 combustion catalog entries and 22 experimental tables containing 2,009 source rows. These remain separate from 78 curated solid-fuel records retained from the project's open-source foundation. Source rows describe different measurements and setups; they are not automatically independent or directly comparable fire tests.

Fifteen research profiles cover investigation families and follow-ups including BASS/BASS-II, Saffire, SAME/SAME-R, FLEX/FLEX-2, ACME, SoFIE-GEL, LUCI, SPICE, SLICE, CFI/CFI-G, E-FIELD and FM2. Users can examine objectives, materials, geometry, apparatus, measurements, findings and limitations. An interactive evidence map, charts and comparison tables make this information easier to navigate.

Research ranking combines the selected safety goal, question similarity, experimental conditions, habitat priorities and evidence availability. Configured local AI supports neural similarity and source-grounded explanations. Ranking components and fallback behavior are disclosed. Scores prioritize research; they do not represent fire probability, detector accuracy or safety certification. Local inference uses Ollama, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Hosted generation requires a separately configured provider.

The modeling workspace supports catalog, ignition and spread-rate data preparation, including source identifiers, exclusions, grouped splits and downloadable datasets. The harmonized PSI view preserves original values and explicit units. Missing, ranged or censored values are flagged rather than invented. Visualizations show oxygen and airflow conditions, reported outcomes and partial-gravity coverage. Exploratory models remain limited by the available evidence.

The intended benefit is to help researchers discover relevant studies, inspect differences and identify missing conditions before planning experiments or developing models. Source-linked application cards also connect the research to smoke detection, fine-water-mist suppression, equipment and potential Earth applications. Independent scientific review remains necessary.

The application uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, CSS and Node.js, with Python for data ingestion and verification. It provides light/dark modes, accessible motion controls, visual reports and downloadable research briefs.

EmberScope extends MIT-licensed MicroFire Atlas by AKM Asifuzzaman. Retained code and curated evidence are credited, with original notices preserved. Our additions include PSI ingestion and harmonization, researcher-focused summaries, research ranking, model-data preparation, applications content, visual reporting and the redesigned interface. OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted development and documentation, and the built-in image tool produced the decorative chamber illustration. Scientific measurements remain linked to their NASA sources.
